heroHeadline: IFT-12 Starship Block 3 Slips Again to NET May 21 — Second Consecutive 24-Hour Delay; S-1 Window Closes May 22
heroSubtitle: 8,779 days of SpaceX milestones — On May 19, 2026, SpaceX announced a second consecutive 24-hour slip for Starship Integrated Flight Test 12 (IFT-12), pushing the No Earlier Than date from May 20 to May 21, 2026 (22:30 UTC / 5:30 p.m. CDT, OLP-2, Starbase). The total cumulative delay from the original NET May 19 target is now 48 hours. SpaceX cited additional system verification time; the fully stacked vehicle (Super Heavy Booster 19 + Ship 39 V3, 124.4 m) remains at OLP-2 with no vehicle anomalies. The revised May 21 window places IFT-12 directly before the close of SpaceX's public S-1 IPO prospectus filing window (May 15–22), consistent with the pre-IPO timeline analysts identified as critical for the $1.75T+ Nasdaq valuation target. IFT-12 objectives: Booster 19 Gulf of Mexico splashdown, Ship 39 V3 Indian Ocean splashdown, 22 Starlink mass-simulator payload deployment, and V3 heat shield thermal imaging by two observer satellites. CRS-34 Cargo Dragon C209 remains docked at ISS Harmony forward port (docked May 17). SpaceX: 58 orbital missions in 2026, 611 total booster recoveries, 10,374+ Starlink satellites in orbit, 10M+ subscribers.
